learnings.question: Which economist and cognitive scientist, in a 1971 observation, argued that a wealth of information creates a scarcity of the attention needed to consume it?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that in an information-rich world, the abundance of information creates a scarcity of attention, since attention is what information consumes.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: In the hadith collection '40 Hadith an-Nawawi,' leaving behind what is described as part of the perfection of a person's Islam?
options: That which does not concern him
learnings.learning: According to Hadith 12 of 40 Hadith an-Nawawi, part of the perfection of one's Islam is leaving that which does not concern him.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist, working in the 1880s, demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned information within 24 hours unless they actively recall it?
learnings.learning: Hermann Ebbinghaus proved in the 1880s that people forget about 80% of what they learn within 24 hours unless they actively force themselves to recall it, which is why spaced repetition and quizzing (not re-reading) work.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: What term describes the phenomenon where people forget information because they trust digital devices to store it for them instead?
learnings.learning: Researchers behind the 'Google Effect' paper call this phenomenon Digital Amnesia: the moment we write something down or store it digitally, our brains treat that as permission to forget it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In the Scrum agile framework, which artifact visualizes the progress of a Sprint and shows how much work remains?
learnings.learning: In Scrum, the Burndown Chart is the artifact that visualizes a Sprint's progress and shows the remaining work, helping the team track whether they are on schedule.

learnings.question: In the Scrum agile framework, what is the primary purpose of breaking a project into short, iterative cycles called Sprints?
options: To increase the overall length of the project
To reduce the number of required team members
To eliminate the need for planning
To allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments
learnings.learning: Scrum breaks a project into iterative cycles called Sprints specifically to allow for more flexibility and quicker adjustments compared to a single long development cycle.

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what Arabic term refers to humanity's role as stewards or caretakers of the Earth?
learnings.learning: Khalifah is the Arabic term for humanity's role as steward or caretaker of the Earth, a responsibility that includes preserving faith and fostering unity.

learnings.question: Which core Islamic concept, affirmed by the verse 'your god is one God' (Quran 2:163), underlies the entire practice of worship in Islam?
learnings.learning: Quran 2:163 affirms that God is one, establishing Tawheed (the oneness of God) as the foundation that worship in Islam is built on.

learnings.question: A central thesis in Islamic theology holds that human purpose revolves around three roles: worshiping God, acting as steward of the Earth, and a third role centered on moral accountability in preparation for what?
learnings.learning: A central framework in Islamic theology holds that human purpose revolves around worship, stewardship of the Earth, and living as a test of faith and conduct in preparation for the Hereafter.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which low-power link state lets a device resume full activity almost instantly after only very short idle periods?
learnings.learning: L0s is a very light PCIe sleep state designed for very short idle periods, allowing the link to quickly wake up and resume full activity.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state puts a device in the deepest sleep — almost completely powered down — giving the greatest power savings but the longest time to resume activity?
learnings.learning: L2 is the deepest PCIe power-saving state, almost completely powering down the device, which maximizes power savings at the cost of the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what term refers to Allah's complete, eternal knowledge and preordained plan for everything that will happen, as distinct from the actual unfolding of events in one's life?
learnings.learning: Qadr is Allah's complete and eternal preordained plan and knowledge of everything that will happen, distinct from Qada', which is the actual unfolding of events as they occur.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: Which surah contains the verse stating that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves?
learnings.learning: Surah Ar-Ra'd (13:11) states that Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves, tying personal change to one's Qada'.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada' and Qadr

learnings.question: When applying the 80/20 Pareto Principle to word frequency in the Quran, what percentage of the text do the top 20 most frequent words actually account for?
learnings.learning: A data analysis of word frequency in the Quran found that the top 20 most repeated words account for only about 20.83% of the text, so the Pareto Principle's 80/20 pattern did not hold.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: What term describes the small diacritical markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds and pronunciation?
learnings.learning: Tashkeel refers to the small diacritical markings placed above or below Arabic letters to indicate vowel sounds, without which Arabic text can be harder to pronounce correctly.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
